resistance_patterns.description: Laws are applied inconsistently depending on political connections of parties involved.

resistance_patterns.name: Asset Seizure Risk
resistance_patterns.description: Successful businesses can attract state or criminal interest leading to asset nationalization or extortion.

opportunity_patterns.name: Shadow Economy Services
opportunity_patterns.description: Large informal economy creates demand for services that operate outside official channels.

opportunity_patterns.name: Consumer Tech in Urban Centers
opportunity_patterns.description: Well-educated urban populations with spending power adopt consumer tech readily.

opportunity_patterns.name: Tech Talent at Discount
opportunity_patterns.description: Highly educated technical talent available at below-market rates due to economic dysfunction.

trust_mechanisms.name: Protection Relationship Network
trust_mechanisms.description: Business is conducted through mutual protection agreements with influential actors.

trust_mechanisms.name: Reputation in Informal Networks
trust_mechanisms.description: Word-of-mouth reputation within informal business networks is the primary trust mechanism.

payment_patterns.name: Cash and Crypto to Avoid Tracking
payment_patterns.description: Cash and cryptocurrency are preferred to avoid taxation and scrutiny.

payment_patterns.name: Barter and Mutual Exchange
payment_patterns.description: Goods and services exchanged directly to avoid formal payment channels.

institutional_patterns.name: Oligarch and Elite Network Capture
institutional_patterns.description: Key sectors controlled by politically connected elites who extract rents.

institutional_patterns.name: Regulatory Arbitrage by Insiders
institutional_patterns.description: Connected actors exploit regulatory gaps unavailable to outsiders.

narrative_patterns.name: Low Profile Survival Narrative
narrative_patterns.description: Successful businesses avoid publicity to prevent attracting official or criminal attention.

narrative_patterns.name: Nationalist Alignment
narrative_patterns.description: Aligning product with national loyalty narratives reduces political risk.

platform_patterns.name: Telegram Business Ecosystem
platform_patterns.description: Telegram is primary secure business and community communication channel.

platform_patterns.name: State-Controlled Payment Rails
platform_patterns.description: Payment systems are monitored by state; transaction data can be accessed by authorities.

regulatory_patterns.name: Law as Weapon
regulatory_patterns.description: Legal system can be weaponized against competitors or foreign businesses.

regulatory_patterns.name: License Denials for Political Reasons
regulatory_patterns.description: Operating licenses in key sectors can be denied or revoked for political reasons.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Distrust of Formal Products
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Decades of institutional betrayal create strong preference for proven informal solutions.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Cash Hoarding and Parallel Currency
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Consumers store value in foreign currency and hard assets rather than domestic banks.

business_model_fit.notes: Only viable for operators who deeply understand informal power dynamics. Formal business models face existential risk.

common_failure_modes.name: Attracting Elite Attention by Success
common_failure_modes.description: Becoming too successful makes a business target for appropriation by powerful actors.

common_failure_modes.name: Formal Legal Route to Dispute Resolution
common_failure_modes.description: Attempting to use courts against politically connected actors fails.

common_success_patterns.name: Operate Under Radar
common_success_patterns.description: Deliberately keeping company size and profile small to avoid attracting attention.

common_success_patterns.name: Protection Relationship Investment
common_success_patterns.description: Investing in relationships with key political and law enforcement figures.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Do Not Enter Without Local Protection Partner
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Never enter without a well-connected local partner who has genuine protection relationships.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Asset-Light Model
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Avoid physical asset ownership that could be seized; use services and software.

source_notes: Based on Russia, Venezuela, Zimbabwe corruption economy characteristics.

name: Infrastructure Deficient
short_description: Economies where unreliable power, roads, internet, and logistics create severe execution friction.
long_description: Infrastructure-deficient economies have failed to build the basic operational infrastructure that other markets take for granted. Power cuts are daily occurrences. Road networks are impassable in rainy season. Internet penetration is low and expensive. Logistics are slow and unreliable. Every business must account for massive infrastructure overhead. The opportunity exists primarily for products that solve these infrastructure problems or work completely within infrastructure constraints.

resistance_patterns.name: Power Outage Operations Disruption
resistance_patterns.description: Daily power cuts of 8-16 hours destroy any business model that requires continuous electricity.

resistance_patterns.name: Last-Mile Logistics Impossibility
resistance_patterns.description: Road conditions make reliable delivery to most of the country impossible.

resistance_patterns.name: Data Cost Barrier
resistance_patterns.description: Mobile data costs are 5-20x higher as % of income compared to developed markets.

opportunity_patterns.name: Infrastructure Gap Filling
opportunity_patterns.description: Products that solve the infrastructure deficit (solar power, offline apps, logistics coordination) have massive demand.

opportunity_patterns.name: Leapfrog Technology Adoption
opportunity_patterns.description: No legacy system to protect means rapid adoption of appropriate technology.

opportunity_patterns.name: Low Competition Landscape
opportunity_patterns.description: Few formal businesses operate; those that solve real problems have limited competition.

trust_mechanisms.name: Physical Presence and Reliability
trust_mechanisms.description: Simply showing up consistently is a major trust differentiator in unreliable environments.

trust_mechanisms.name: Community Network Vouching
trust_mechanisms.description: Community networks are the only reliable trust transmission mechanism.

payment_patterns.name: Mobile Money as Primary Rail
payment_patterns.description: Orange Money, Airtel Money growing as primary formal payment channels.

payment_patterns.name: Barter and Informal Exchange
payment_patterns.description: Significant proportion of transactions use barter or informal goods exchange.

institutional_patterns.name: NGO as Primary Service Provider
institutional_patterns.description: NGOs deliver health, education, and infrastructure services state cannot provide.

institutional_patterns.name: Customary Law Over Formal Law
institutional_patterns.description: Community-based customary law often more effective than formal legal system.

narrative_patterns.name: Solving Daily Suffering
narrative_patterns.description: Products that visibly reduce daily suffering (power, water, connectivity) have instant narrative value.

narrative_patterns.name: International Donor Legitimacy
narrative_patterns.description: UN, World Bank, or bilateral donor association provides external credibility.

platform_patterns.name: SMS and Radio Primary Channels
platform_patterns.description: SMS and community radio remain primary mass communication channels.

platform_patterns.name: Facebook as Internet for Many
platform_patterns.description: Facebook Basics and WhatsApp function as primary internet for many users.

regulatory_patterns.name: Regulatory Capacity Absence
regulatory_patterns.description: Governments lack capacity to enforce regulations; compliance is largely voluntary.

regulatory_patterns.name: International Standards Required by Donors
regulatory_patterns.description: Products funded by donors must meet international standards (WASH, medical devices).

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Survival Spending Priority
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Spending decisions dominated by immediate survival needs before any discretionary purchasing.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Product Must Work in Conditions
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Any product must function without reliable power, internet, or logistics support.

business_model_fit.notes: Only viable with radically simplified, offline-capable, resilient product design.

common_failure_modes.name: Assuming Smartphone Connectivity
common_failure_modes.description: Building any product that requires reliable internet access.

common_failure_modes.name: Underestimating Generator and Solar Costs
common_failure_modes.description: Not factoring infrastructure costs into unit economics.

common_success_patterns.name: Solar Plus Digital Bundle
common_success_patterns.description: Combining solar power with digital access creates bundled infrastructure solution.

common_success_patterns.name: Batch Processing Design
common_success_patterns.description: Systems that process data in batches when connectivity is available, not real-time.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Partner with Energy Provider
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Partner with solar or generator supplier to bundle access to power.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Radical Simplification First
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Strip product to absolute minimum viable function before worrying about features.

source_notes: Based on Liberia, CAR, Madagascar infrastructure characteristics.

name: Urban Poverty
short_description: Dense urban slums and informal settlements with survival spending, high social density, and community resilience.
long_description: Urban poverty economies exist within larger urban economies but in informal settlements, slums, and low-income neighborhoods where formal economic infrastructure barely reaches. These areas have high population density, complex social networks, and significant social entrepreneurship energy. Smartphone penetration is moderate. The challenge is income levels, not ambition.
core_characteristic: Dense cities, survival spending, high social pressure

resistance_patterns.name: Income Below Viable Threshold
resistance_patterns.description: Most residents cannot afford any non-essential spending; unit economics rarely work.

resistance_patterns.name: Informal Settlement Legal Status
resistance_patterns.description: Land and property rights are informal; businesses operating in settlements lack legal protection.

resistance_patterns.name: Crime and Safety Risk
resistance_patterns.description: Crime rates are high; physical delivery, installation, or operations face real safety risk.

opportunity_patterns.name: Community Service Platforms
opportunity_patterns.description: Dense populations sharing problems create demand for community-scaled solutions.

opportunity_patterns.name: Micro-Entrepreneur Tooling
opportunity_patterns.description: Large number of micro-entrepreneurs need affordable business tools, credit, and distribution.

opportunity_patterns.name: Youth Talent Pool
opportunity_patterns.description: Young, educated, and unemployed population is available for work at low cost.

trust_mechanisms.name: Community Leader Endorsement
trust_mechanisms.description: Community associations, savings groups, and religious leaders are primary trust channels.

trust_mechanisms.name: Peer Group Demonstration
trust_mechanisms.description: Product adoption happens in groups; one adopter in a peer group triggers cluster adoption.

payment_patterns.name: Daily Income Micro-Payments
payment_patterns.description: Income arrives daily, so payment models must accommodate daily micro-payment sizes.

payment_patterns.name: Mobile Money Growing
payment_patterns.description: M-Pesa, bKash, GoPay growing as primary formal payment rails.

institutional_patterns.name: Community Association Governance
institutional_patterns.description: Informal community associations (RWAs, market committees) are de facto local government.

institutional_patterns.name: State Welfare Programs
institutional_patterns.description: Government welfare programs (PDS, NREGA) are significant household income source.

narrative_patterns.name: Dignity and Aspiration
narrative_patterns.description: Products that help users achieve dignity and progress rather than highlighting poverty.

narrative_patterns.name: Neighborhood Success Story
narrative_patterns.description: Local success stories spread virally within communities.

platform_patterns.name: WhatsApp Community Groups
platform_patterns.description: WhatsApp groups function as primary community information and commerce channel.

platform_patterns.name: Kirana Network
platform_patterns.description: Local small shop (kirana) networks function as last-mile distribution infrastructure.

regulatory_patterns.name: Informal Settlement Lack of Address
regulatory_patterns.description: No formal address system in many settlements; delivery and legal identity systems fail.

regulatory_patterns.name: Eviction Risk for Physical Businesses
regulatory_patterns.description: Government demolition programs can destroy physical business infrastructure overnight.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Value Above All Else
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Every purchase is a serious trade-off against essential spending; value must be overwhelming.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Group Buying and Sharing
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Products and services are often shared among multiple households.

business_model_fit.notes: Only viable with extreme cost optimization and community distribution model.

common_failure_modes.name: Non-Essential Product at Non-Survival Price
common_failure_modes.description: Any product priced above survival budget fails regardless of quality.

common_failure_modes.name: Middle-Class Product Design
common_failure_modes.description: Designing for middle-class use patterns and assuming low-income users will adapt.

common_success_patterns.name: Daily or Weekly Payment Model
common_success_patterns.description: Accepting daily or weekly micropayments rather than monthly or annual billing.

common_success_patterns.name: Community Agent Model
common_success_patterns.description: Training community members as paid agents to distribute and support products.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: FMCG Distribution Partnership
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Partner with FMCG companies that already have last-mile distribution to informal settlements.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Savings Group Integration
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Integrate product with existing savings groups (Chama, SHG) for built-in distribution.

source_notes: Based on urban poverty characteristics in India, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Kenya.

name: Black Market War
short_description: Active conflict zones where underground commerce, smuggling, and survival economics dominate.
long_description: Black market war economies exist in active conflict zones where formal economic structures have collapsed. Commerce is dominated by smuggling, black market currency exchange, and informal armed actor taxation of trade routes. Population displacement is ongoing. Life and property are at daily risk. No viable commercial business model exists here except for humanitarian operations, communications infrastructure, and conflict-aware logistics.

resistance_patterns.name: Active Physical Security Threat
resistance_patterns.description: Staff, assets, and customers face daily physical security threats.

resistance_patterns.name: Zero Institutional Infrastructure
resistance_patterns.description: Courts, banks, government agencies, and utilities have ceased to function.

resistance_patterns.name: Forced Taxation by Armed Actors
resistance_patterns.description: Armed groups impose levies on all commercial activity in territory they control.

opportunity_patterns.name: Humanitarian Communication Needs
opportunity_patterns.description: Population needs communications, coordination, and access to information.

opportunity_patterns.name: Diaspora Remittance Flow
opportunity_patterns.description: Large displaced populations sending money home through hawala and informal channels.

opportunity_patterns.name: Post-Conflict Reconstruction Opportunity
opportunity_patterns.description: Future reconstruction will require massive technology and infrastructure investment.

trust_mechanisms.name: Armed Faction Protection
trust_mechanisms.description: Business operates only with protection guarantee from dominant armed faction.

trust_mechanisms.name: Hawala Network Trust
trust_mechanisms.description: Centuries-old hawala trust network remains functional when all else collapses.

payment_patterns.name: USD Cash and Gold
payment_patterns.description: Only USD cash and gold are stable value stores in active conflict.

payment_patterns.name: Hawala Informal Remittance
payment_patterns.description: Hawala is the primary reliable cross-border value transfer mechanism.

institutional_patterns.name: Armed Faction as De Facto Authority
institutional_patterns.description: Armed factions control territory and determine what business activities are permitted.

institutional_patterns.name: International Aid Coordination as Order
institutional_patterns.description: OCHA and UN coordination is often the only functioning coordination mechanism.

narrative_patterns.name: Survival Communication
narrative_patterns.description: Communication about safety, location, and survival resources dominates all attention.

narrative_patterns.name: Resistance or Faction Identity
narrative_patterns.description: Business must align with or at least not threaten dominant faction identity.

platform_patterns.name: Telegram for Secure Communication
platform_patterns.description: Telegram is primary secure communication platform in conflict zones.

platform_patterns.name: Satellite Internet for Connectivity
platform_patterns.description: Starlink and VSAT are only reliable internet options.

regulatory_patterns.name: No Functioning Legal System
regulatory_patterns.description: No functioning courts or enforcement mechanisms for commercial disputes.

regulatory_patterns.name: Sanctions Complexity
regulatory_patterns.description: International sanctions may apply to transactions with certain factions or territories.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Survival-Only Spending
customer_behavior_patterns.description: All spending oriented toward immediate survival; no discretionary commerce.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Armed Protection Required for Commerce
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Market activities require protection arrangement with armed actors.

business_model_fit.notes: Extremely limited commercial opportunity. Only humanitarian and communications businesses viable.

common_failure_modes.name: Assuming Rule of Law
common_failure_modes.description: Any business plan that assumes contracts, property rights, or legal protection will fail.

common_failure_modes.name: Staff Safety Miscalculation
common_failure_modes.description: Underestimating security risk leads to staff casualties and operation collapse.

common_success_patterns.name: Remote Operations Only
common_success_patterns.description: Technology operations that require zero physical presence.

common_success_patterns.name: Faction Neutrality
common_success_patterns.description: Maintaining strict neutrality between competing factions is critical for any operation.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Do Not Enter Without Security Plan
recommended_entry_strategies.description: No commercial or humanitarian operation should enter without detailed security protocol.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Remote Technology Support Only
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Support local operators remotely rather than deploying staff.

name: Occupied Territory
short_description: Externally controlled territories with movement restrictions, permit systems, and suppressed economic autonomy.
long_description: Occupied territory economies face the challenge of operating under external political and military control. Freedom of movement is restricted. Permits are required for most commercial activities. Import/export is controlled by the occupying power. Despite this, internal economic resilience is significant, driven by community solidarity and parallel informal systems.

resistance_patterns.name: Movement and Trade Restrictions
resistance_patterns.description: Physical movement of people and goods requires permits from occupying authorities.

resistance_patterns.name: Currency and Banking Dependency
resistance_patterns.description: Dependent on occupying power's currency and banking system; limited monetary autonomy.

resistance_patterns.name: Infrastructure Destruction Risk
resistance_patterns.description: Infrastructure can be destroyed in military operations, eliminating business assets overnight.

opportunity_patterns.name: Digital Services Bypass Physical Restrictions
opportunity_patterns.description: Software, digital services, and remote work bypass physical movement restrictions.

opportunity_patterns.name: Diaspora Economic Connection
opportunity_patterns.description: Large diaspora maintains economic links and remittance flows.

opportunity_patterns.name: Tech Talent for Export
opportunity_patterns.description: Highly educated population builds tech skills for export to global markets.

trust_mechanisms.name: National Solidarity Network
trust_mechanisms.description: Community solidarity is extremely high; trust within community is strong.

trust_mechanisms.name: Family and Clan Networks
trust_mechanisms.description: Extended family and clan networks are primary business trust frameworks.

payment_patterns.name: Israeli Shekel and JD Dependency
payment_patterns.description: Primary currency depends on occupying/adjacent power.

payment_patterns.name: Hawala Cross-Border Transfers
payment_patterns.description: Hawala used for cross-border value transfers where banking is restricted.

institutional_patterns.name: Parallel Governance Structures
institutional_patterns.description: Both occupying authority and resistance governance structures impose requirements.

institutional_patterns.name: International Donor Support
institutional_patterns.description: International development organizations provide significant economic support.

narrative_patterns.name: Resistance and Sumud (Steadfastness)
narrative_patterns.description: Business framed as act of economic resistance and community preservation.

narrative_patterns.name: International Solidarity Market
narrative_patterns.description: Global community of supporters creates market for Palestinian products.

platform_patterns.name: Social Media Activism Platform
platform_patterns.description: Social media simultaneously an activism tool and a commerce platform.

platform_patterns.name: Zoom and Remote Work Platforms
platform_patterns.description: Video conferencing enables global work despite physical restrictions.

regulatory_patterns.name: Dual Legal System Complexity
regulatory_patterns.description: Both PA law and Israeli military orders apply simultaneously.

regulatory_patterns.name: Import Approval Requirements
regulatory_patterns.description: Importing goods requires clearance from multiple authorities.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Buy Palestinian Preference
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Strong community preference for purchasing from Palestinian suppliers.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Crisis-Resilient Consumer Habits
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Consumer habits shaped by experience of sudden economic shock and closure.

business_model_fit.notes: Digital services and remote work are the most viable commercial models.

common_failure_modes.name: Physical Asset Investment
common_failure_modes.description: Investing in physical assets that can be destroyed or inaccessible.

common_failure_modes.name: Assuming Stable Operating Environment
common_failure_modes.description: Any plan assuming stable conditions will be disrupted.

common_success_patterns.name: Digital-Only Business Model
common_success_patterns.description: Pure digital products and services avoid physical risk entirely.

common_success_patterns.name: Export Market Focus
common_success_patterns.description: Focusing on international markets reduces dependency on constrained local economy.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Remote Business Model First
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Design business to operate without requiring physical presence or movement.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Partner with Palestinian Tech Ecosystem
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Engage with Gaza Sky Geeks, Ramallah Hub, and local tech ecosystem.

short_description: Countries in active civil conflict with fractured authority, currency collapse, and mass displacement.

Currency may have collapsed or multiple currencies operate simultaneously. Economic activity continues at a survival level but formal commerce is nearly impossible. Humanitarian operations are the primary functioning economic system.

resistance_patterns.name: Complete Institutional Collapse
resistance_patterns.description: All government institutions, courts, banks, and utilities have ceased functioning.

resistance_patterns.name: Population Displacement
resistance_patterns.description: Mass displacement creates unstable customer base and disrupted supply chains.

resistance_patterns.name: Currency Hyperinflation
resistance_patterns.description: National currency has collapsed or is hyperinflating; pricing is impossible.

opportunity_patterns.name: Humanitarian Technology
opportunity_patterns.description: UNHCR, WFP, and ICRC operations require coordination, data, and communication tools.

opportunity_patterns.name: Diaspora Remittance
opportunity_patterns.description: Large diaspora sending value to displaced family members.

opportunity_patterns.name: Post-War Reconstruction
opportunity_patterns.description: Long-term reconstruction creates future investment opportunity.

trust_mechanisms.name: Ethnic and Family Networks
trust_mechanisms.description: Trust operates exclusively through ethnic, clan, and family networks.

trust_mechanisms.name: Armed Faction Guarantee
trust_mechanisms.description: Business conducted only with protection guarantee from dominant local faction.

payment_patterns.name: USD Cash Exclusively
payment_patterns.description: Only USD or gold are accepted as stores of value.

payment_patterns.name: Barter for Daily Needs
payment_patterns.description: Daily needs transacted through barter.

institutional_patterns.name: Multiple Competing Authorities
institutional_patterns.description: Different armed groups control different areas; any business must manage multiple authority relationships.

institutional_patterns.description: UN agencies are the only broadly accepted neutral coordination bodies.

narrative_patterns.name: Faction Neutrality Essential
narrative_patterns.description: Any communication that takes sides in the conflict creates existential risk.

narrative_patterns.name: Humanitarian Mission as Shield
narrative_patterns.description: Humanitarian mission framing provides some protection and access.

platform_patterns.name: Telegram and Encrypted Messaging
platform_patterns.description: Encrypted messaging is primary communication; open communications are dangerous.

platform_patterns.name: Satellite for Connectivity
platform_patterns.description: Satellite internet is only reliable connectivity in active conflict zones.

regulatory_patterns.name: No Functioning Legal System
regulatory_patterns.description: Courts do not function; no legal recourse for any dispute.

regulatory_patterns.name: War Crime and Sanctions Exposure
regulatory_patterns.description: Engagement with certain actors may violate international law or sanctions.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Pure Survival Spending
customer_behavior_patterns.description: All spending directed to immediate survival.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Asset Preservation Behavior
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Remaining assets being protected and hidden; no investment.

business_model_fit.notes: No viable commercial business models. Only humanitarian operations.

common_failure_modes.name: Commercial Business Model Attempt
common_failure_modes.description: Any attempt at commercial business in active civil war zones.

common_failure_modes.name: Side Selection
common_failure_modes.description: Any perceived alignment with one faction makes organization target for others.

common_success_patterns.name: UN System Alignment
common_success_patterns.description: Operating exclusively within UN coordination system.

common_success_patterns.name: Remote Operations Only
common_success_patterns.description: All operations managed remotely with no physical presence.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Do Not Enter
recommended_entry_strategies.description: No commercial organization should enter active civil war zones.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Pre-Position for Post-Conflict
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Build relationships with diaspora and civil society for post-conflict entry.

source_notes: Based on Sudan, Myanmar civil conflict characteristics.

name: Militia Controlled
short_description: Territories where armed non-state groups impose taxation, control trade routes, and extract economic rents.
long_description: Militia-controlled economies exist in territories where non-state armed groups have displaced government authority. Militias impose taxes on trade routes, extort businesses, and control access to resources. Life under militia control is possible but operates under constant threat. Economic activity exists but all profits are subject to forced extraction.
core_characteristic: Armed group taxation, coercion, route capture
countries: Parts of Democratic Republic of Congo

resistance_patterns.name: Forced Taxation on All Commerce
resistance_patterns.description: Militias impose arbitrary levies on all trade; profit margins are unpredictable.

resistance_patterns.name: Zero Property Rights
resistance_patterns.description: Property can be seized by militia forces at any time.

resistance_patterns.name: Route Monopoly Control
resistance_patterns.description: Militias control road and market access; logistics impossible without compliance.

opportunity_patterns.name: Mineral Resource Access
opportunity_patterns.description: Parts of DRC and Somalia have valuable mineral resources despite instability.

opportunity_patterns.name: Humanitarian Operations Required
opportunity_patterns.description: Population needs require humanitarian operations regardless of militia presence.

opportunity_patterns.name: Mobile Connectivity Entry
opportunity_patterns.description: Mobile network operators negotiate access rights with militias for signal towers.

trust_mechanisms.name: Militia Protection Payment
trust_mechanisms.description: Business operates only through payment of protection fees to militia.

trust_mechanisms.name: Community Clan Networks
trust_mechanisms.description: Within communities, clan and family networks maintain trust despite external chaos.

payment_patterns.name: Cash in Dominant Currency
payment_patterns.description: USD, gold, or local stable currency for all transactions.

payment_patterns.name: Resource-for-Goods Barter
payment_patterns.description: Mineral resources exchanged for goods and services.

institutional_patterns.name: Militia as Tax Authority
institutional_patterns.description: Militia serves as de facto tax and regulatory authority.

institutional_patterns.name: International NGO as Service State
institutional_patterns.description: NGOs provide education, health, and food services that government cannot.

narrative_patterns.name: Neutrality is Survival
narrative_patterns.description: Appearing neutral to all militia factions is critical.

narrative_patterns.name: Humanitarian Framing for Access
narrative_patterns.description: Humanitarian identity provides access that commercial identity does not.

platform_patterns.name: Radio for Mass Communication
platform_patterns.description: Radio remains primary mass communication in militia-controlled territories.

platform_patterns.name: Encrypted Satellite Communication
platform_patterns.description: Satellite phones and encrypted messaging essential for coordination.

regulatory_patterns.name: No Government Law
regulatory_patterns.description: Government law does not apply; militia rules are the only enforceable framework.

regulatory_patterns.name: International Humanitarian Law
regulatory_patterns.description: IHL applies in theory; practical enforcement is absent.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Survival Prioritized
customer_behavior_patterns.description: All spending oriented to immediate survival.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Militia-Approved Commerce Only
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Only products and services approved (explicitly or implicitly) by militia can be sold.

business_model_fit.notes: No commercial business models viable. Humanitarian operations only.

common_failure_modes.name: Attempting Commercial Operations
common_failure_modes.description: All commercial operations fail due to militia extraction.

common_failure_modes.name: Single Militia Relationship
common_failure_modes.description: Building relationship with one militia and being vulnerable when balance of power shifts.

common_success_patterns.name: Multi-Faction Negotiation
common_success_patterns.description: Organizations that successfully negotiate access with all factions survive longer.

common_success_patterns.name: Remote Operations Only
common_success_patterns.description: Physical presence minimized to reduce extraction exposure.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Do Not Enter Without Security Specialist
recommended_entry_strategies.description: No organization should enter without experienced humanitarian security advisor.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: UN OCHA Coordination First
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Enter through UN OCHA coordination mechanisms only.

source_notes: Based on DRC and Somali militia economy characteristics.

name: Sanctioned
short_description: Economies cut off from international financial systems with underground alternatives and resource constraints.
long_description: Sanctioned economies face significant restrictions on international payments, imports, and access to global financial infrastructure. Businesses develop underground alternatives — cryptocurrency, hawala, barter, third-country intermediaries. Innovation continues despite sanctions, particularly in workaround technology. Exports are limited, imports are expensive. The domestic market is the primary addressable market.
core_characteristic: Blocked payments, restricted imports, underground alternatives

resistance_patterns.name: International Payment Impossibility
resistance_patterns.description: SWIFT exclusion and sanctions make all international financial transactions extremely difficult.

resistance_patterns.name: Import and Tech Restriction
resistance_patterns.description: Critical imports — semiconductors, software, hardware — are blocked or severely restricted.

resistance_patterns.name: Secondary Sanctions Risk
resistance_patterns.description: Third parties transacting with sanctioned entities face secondary sanctions from US/EU.

opportunity_patterns.name: Import Substitution Technology
opportunity_patterns.description: Massive government demand for domestic alternatives to sanctioned imports.

opportunity_patterns.name: Cryptocurrency and Workaround Finance
opportunity_patterns.description: Domestic crypto adoption and hawala networks create new payment infrastructure.

opportunity_patterns.name: Domestic Market Captivity
opportunity_patterns.description: Sanctions reduce competition from foreign products, protecting domestic producers.

trust_mechanisms.name: State Endorsement Critical
trust_mechanisms.description: Government certification or endorsement required for large B2B contracts.

trust_mechanisms.name: Informal Network Trust
trust_mechanisms.description: Personal networks and informal trust critical since formal institutions compromised.

payment_patterns.name: Crypto and Hawala Alternatives
payment_patterns.description: Cryptocurrency and hawala are primary cross-border payment mechanisms.

payment_patterns.name: State Banking Forced Usage
payment_patterns.description: Domestic transactions forced through state-controlled banking system.

institutional_patterns.name: State Direction of Economy
institutional_patterns.description: Government directs investment toward sanctioned sectors as national priority.

institutional_patterns.name: Revolutionary Guard / Parastatal Control
institutional_patterns.description: Key economic sectors controlled by security apparatus or government parastatals.

narrative_patterns.name: National Resistance Narrative
narrative_patterns.description: Framing business as contributing to national resistance against sanctions.

narrative_patterns.name: Self-Sufficiency Achievement
narrative_patterns.description: Narrative of achieving self-sufficiency resonates with government and public.

platform_patterns.name: Domestic Social Platforms
platform_patterns.description: Domestic alternatives to banned platforms (RuTube, Aparat) with state-controlled content.

platform_patterns.name: VPN and Circumvention Tools
platform_patterns.description: VPN usage is high despite official restrictions; significant portion accesses banned content.

regulatory_patterns.name: Customs Circumvention Mechanisms
regulatory_patterns.description: Complex parallel import systems legally or semi-legally circumvent trade restrictions.

regulatory_patterns.name: State Procurement Dominance
regulatory_patterns.description: State is the primary customer for major goods and services.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Workaround Culture
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Consumers are highly skilled at finding workarounds for blocked services.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: State Approved Alternatives
customer_behavior_patterns.description: For sensitive categories, consumers use only state-approved alternatives.

business_model_fit.notes: Only domestic-focused businesses viable. International business almost impossible.

common_failure_modes.name: Assuming Payment Will Work
common_failure_modes.description: Any assumption that international payment will function reliably.

common_failure_modes.name: Secondary Sanctions Exposure
common_failure_modes.description: Third-country businesses that fail to check sanctions compliance face asset freezes.

common_success_patterns.name: Full Domestic Business Model
common_success_patterns.description: Businesses that operate entirely within domestic economy avoid sanctions risk.

common_success_patterns.name: Government Contract as Revenue Base
common_success_patterns.description: State procurement provides stable, domestic-currency revenue base.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Do Not Enter Without Legal Counsel
recommended_entry_strategies.description: International businesses must get comprehensive sanctions legal opinion before any activity.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Local Partner with Government Access
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Local partner with established government relationships.

source_notes: Based on Iran, North Korea, Russia post-2022 sanction characteristics.

name: Post Collapse
short_description: Economies recovering from institutional failure with barter systems, survival networks, and minimal formal commerce.
long_description: Post-collapse economies exist after a period of total or near-total institutional failure. Formal economy has collapsed; informal survival economy has taken over. Barter, community sharing, and informal credit based on trust are the primary economic mechanisms. Reconstruction is happening but slowly. Haiti after 2010 and the COVID-19 aftermath in some economies are examples. Basic survival is the economic priority.

resistance_patterns.name: Zero Institutional Infrastructure
resistance_patterns.description: No functioning courts, banks, government services, or formal infrastructure.

resistance_patterns.name: Security and Gang Control
resistance_patterns.description: Armed gangs control significant areas and impose economic extraction.

resistance_patterns.name: No Formal Payment System
resistance_patterns.description: No functioning banking; cash-only with no reliable currency.

opportunity_patterns.name: Reconstruction Demand
opportunity_patterns.description: Post-collapse reconstruction creates demand for basic infrastructure and services.

opportunity_patterns.name: Community Resilience Networks
opportunity_patterns.description: Community solidarity networks are highly functional and can be leveraged for distribution.

opportunity_patterns.name: International Development Investment
opportunity_patterns.description: Post-collapse states attract significant international reconstruction funding.

trust_mechanisms.name: Community Elder and Religious Leadership
trust_mechanisms.description: Church leaders and community elders are primary trust figures.

trust_mechanisms.name: NGO Affiliation
trust_mechanisms.description: Affiliation with recognized international NGO provides protection and trust.

payment_patterns.name: US Dollar Cash Only
payment_patterns.description: USD cash is the only reliable payment medium.

payment_patterns.name: Barter for Local Goods
payment_patterns.description: Local goods and services traded by barter.

institutional_patterns.name: NGO as Parallel Government
institutional_patterns.description: International NGOs provide services the government cannot.

institutional_patterns.name: Gang Territory Control
institutional_patterns.description: Gang networks control territory and extract economic rents.

narrative_patterns.name: Reconstruction and Hope
narrative_patterns.description: Narratives of hope and reconstruction resonate with diaspora and international donors.

narrative_patterns.name: Community Dignity
narrative_patterns.description: Framing around dignity and community agency rather than charity.

platform_patterns.name: WhatsApp for Emergency Coordination
platform_patterns.description: WhatsApp is primary coordination tool where connectivity exists.

platform_patterns.name: Radio for Mass Communication
platform_patterns.description: Radio reaches populations without smartphones or internet.

regulatory_patterns.name: Weak or Absent Law
regulatory_patterns.description: Legal system functions minimally or not at all.

regulatory_patterns.name: International Standards Required
regulatory_patterns.description: Aid organizations impose their own standards as de facto regulation.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Pure Survival Mode
customer_behavior_patterns.description: All decisions oriented toward immediate survival.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Community Sharing Norm
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Goods are shared within community groups; private ownership norms are weakened.

business_model_fit.notes: Only humanitarian and reconstruction operations viable.

common_failure_modes.name: Commercial Business Assumptions
common_failure_modes.description: Assuming any normal commercial infrastructure will function.

common_failure_modes.name: Ignoring Gang Risk
common_failure_modes.description: Underestimating armed group control of territory.

common_success_patterns.name: Community-Led Service Delivery
common_success_patterns.description: Services delivered through and by community members succeed where external-led efforts fail.

common_success_patterns.name: Cash Transfer Programs
common_success_patterns.description: Direct cash transfers to households more effective than in-kind aid.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: NGO or UN Partnership First
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Enter through established humanitarian organizations as primary partners.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Diaspora-Led Entry
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Diaspora members with family networks provide trusted entry pathway.

source_notes: Based on Haiti and Somali post-collapse characteristics.

name: Creator Economy
short_description: Attention-driven digital economies where personal brands, algorithms, and content monetization determine success.
long_description: The creator economy is a global attention marketplace operating across YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Twitch, and emerging platforms. Revenue flows through ads, sponsorships, memberships, merchandise, and courses. Success is determined by algorithm performance, audience attention capture, and platform relationship management. Reputation is fragile and can collapse overnight. The market is simultaneously global and hyper-niche.

resistance_patterns.name: Algorithm Dependency and Volatility
resistance_patterns.description: Revenue completely dependent on platform algorithms that change without notice.

resistance_patterns.name: Audience Attention Fragmentation
resistance_patterns.description: Audience attention is constantly competing with thousands of other creators.

resistance_patterns.name: Platform Policy Risk
resistance_patterns.description: Demonetization, shadow banning, and policy changes can eliminate income overnight.

opportunity_patterns.name: Global Niche Monetization
opportunity_patterns.description: Every niche has a global audience large enough to sustain a creator business.

opportunity_patterns.name: Multiple Revenue Stream Architecture
opportunity_patterns.description: Diversified revenue (ads, sponsors, memberships, merch, courses) creates resilience.

opportunity_patterns.name: Creator Tool Market
opportunity_patterns.description: Massive demand for editing, scheduling, analytics, and monetization tools from 50M+ creators.

trust_mechanisms.name: Parasocial Relationship
trust_mechanisms.description: Audience develops parasocial relationships with creators; personal trust is the product.

trust_mechanisms.name: Authenticity Signal
trust_mechanisms.description: Perceived authenticity is the primary trust currency; corporate behavior destroys trust.

payment_patterns.name: Platform Revenue Share
payment_patterns.description: Primary revenue via YouTube AdSense, TikTok Creator Fund, etc.

payment_patterns.name: Stripe and Direct Membership
payment_patterns.description: Substack, Patreon, and direct Stripe billing for premium content.

institutional_patterns.name: Platform as Regulator
institutional_patterns.description: YouTube, TikTok, and Meta set and enforce content rules — effectively as regulators.

institutional_patterns.name: MCN and Talent Management
institutional_patterns.description: Multi-channel networks and talent managers negotiate deals and provide support.

narrative_patterns.name: Personal Story as Brand
narrative_patterns.description: Creator's personal journey IS the brand narrative; authenticity is the product.

narrative_patterns.name: Community Identity
narrative_patterns.description: Successful creators build community identities (fandom names, inside jokes, rituals).

platform_patterns.name: YouTube Primary for Long-Form
platform_patterns.description: YouTube dominates long-form discovery and monetization.

platform_patterns.name: TikTok for Short-Form Discovery
platform_patterns.description: TikTok is primary short-form discovery engine for new audience growth.

regulatory_patterns.name: FTC Disclosure Requirements
regulatory_patterns.description: Sponsored content must be disclosed; failure creates legal and reputational risk.

regulatory_patterns.name: Copyright and DMCA
regulatory_patterns.description: Music and content copyright claims can demonetize or remove creator content.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Attention Follows Entertainment + Value
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Audiences follow creators who entertain or provide clear value; education alone is not enough.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Tribal Community Participation
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Fans want to participate in community, not just consume.

business_model_fit.notes: Optimal for creator tools, membership platforms, and creator education businesses.

common_failure_modes.name: Single Platform Dependency
common_failure_modes.description: Depending on one platform for all revenue and audience.

common_failure_modes.name: Audience Mismatch with Monetization
common_failure_modes.description: Building large audience in demographic that doesn't match sponsorship or purchase behavior.

common_success_patterns.name: Own the Email List
common_success_patterns.description: Building owned email list and newsletter independent of platform algorithms.

common_success_patterns.name: Diversified Revenue Stack
common_success_patterns.description: Building 5+ revenue streams (ads, sponsors, memberships, courses, merch, services).

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Niche Domination Before Broadening
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Dominate one specific niche before expanding to broader topics.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Cross-Platform Presence from Day One
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Build simultaneously on 2-3 platforms to avoid single-platform dependency.

source_notes: Based on creator economy characteristics in USA, South Korea, Brazil.

name: Gig Platform
short_description: App-mediated flexible labor economies where platform algorithms control access to work.
long_description: Gig platform economies are built around algorithmic labor marketplaces where platform companies match demand with supply of flexible workers. Uber, DoorDash, Bolt, TaskRabbit, and similar platforms have created a new labor category. Workers have flexibility but face algorithmic control, volatile earnings, and lack of benefits. Platform companies capture value through percentage fees.
core_characteristic: App-based work, flexible labor, platform control

resistance_patterns.name: Platform Lock-In and Fee Extraction
resistance_patterns.description: Platform takes 20-35% of all transactions; worker margins are thin.

resistance_patterns.name: Worker Classification Legal Risk
resistance_patterns.description: Gig worker vs employee classification battles in multiple jurisdictions.

resistance_patterns.name: Cold Start Problem
resistance_patterns.description: Two-sided marketplace requires simultaneous worker and customer density to function.

opportunity_patterns.name: Underserved Service Categories
opportunity_patterns.description: Many service categories still lack efficient digital matching platforms.

opportunity_patterns.name: Worker Income Diversification Tools
opportunity_patterns.description: Workers using multiple platforms need management tools.

opportunity_patterns.name: B2B Flex Staffing Automation
opportunity_patterns.description: Enterprise flex staffing solutions using gig worker infrastructure.

trust_mechanisms.name: Star Rating System
trust_mechanisms.description: Bidirectional star ratings are primary trust mechanism for both workers and customers.

trust_mechanisms.name: Identity Verification
trust_mechanisms.description: Background checks and ID verification provide safety trust signals.

payment_patterns.name: In-App Payment Mandatory
payment_patterns.description: All transactions handled in-app; cash payments are platform policy violation.

payment_patterns.name: Instant Pay Options Growing
payment_patterns.description: Workers increasingly demanding instant or daily payout options.

institutional_patterns.name: Platform as Labor Market
institutional_patterns.description: Platforms function as labor markets, setting prices, allocating work, and managing quality.

institutional_patterns.name: Regulatory Pressure on Classification
institutional_patterns.description: AB5 (California), Uber UK ruling, EU gig law create employment reclassification pressure.

narrative_patterns.name: Flexibility and Freedom Narrative
narrative_patterns.description: Marketing to workers emphasizes flexibility and being your own boss.

narrative_patterns.name: Convenience and On-Demand Narrative
narrative_patterns.description: Marketing to customers emphasizes convenience and instant availability.

platform_patterns.name: Google Maps Integration
platform_patterns.description: Navigation and location services are core platform infrastructure.

platform_patterns.name: App Store and Play Store Dependency
platform_patterns.description: Entirely dependent on Apple and Google app distribution.

regulatory_patterns.name: Worker Misclassification Liability
regulatory_patterns.description: Reclassification of workers as employees creates massive cost exposure.

regulatory_patterns.name: City-Level Transport Regulations
regulatory_patterns.description: Ride-sharing and delivery regulated at city level with varying requirements.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Price Sensitivity and Surge Resistance
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Customers abandon platforms during price surges; price elasticity is high.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: App Switching Behavior
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Customers use multiple competing platforms to find best price/availability.

business_model_fit.notes: Ideal for gig labor infrastructure, worker tools, and B2B flex staffing.

common_failure_modes.name: Geographic Density Failure
common_failure_modes.description: Launching in too many cities simultaneously, achieving critical mass nowhere.

common_failure_modes.name: Race to Zero Pricing
common_failure_modes.description: Competing on price until margins are destroyed for both platform and workers.

common_success_patterns.name: Single City Critical Mass First
common_success_patterns.description: Achieve undeniable density in one city before geographic expansion.

common_success_patterns.name: Supply Side First Strategy
common_success_patterns.description: Signing up and subsidizing workers first to ensure service availability before demand push.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Vertical Specialization
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Enter one specific service vertical deeply rather than competing with Uber/DoorDash broadly.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Worker Benefits as Differentiator
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Offering worker benefits (insurance, income stability) as differentiation against incumbents.

source_notes: Based on global gig economy characteristics in USA, India, Indonesia.

name: Freelance Digital
short_description: Global remote services economy where skilled workers compete for international clients on digital platforms.
long_description: The freelance digital economy is a global labor marketplace for knowledge workers — software developers, designers, writers, marketers, and consultants. Upwork, Fiverr, Toptal, and LinkedIn connect workers from lower-income countries with clients in higher-income markets. Platform fee structures (10-20%) and reputation systems govern the market. Income arbitrage between labor markets creates significant opportunity for skilled workers in emerging economies.

resistance_patterns.name: Platform Reputation Cold Start
resistance_patterns.description: New freelancers face impossible task of getting first review without prior reviews.

resistance_patterns.name: Race to Bottom on Pricing
resistance_patterns.description: High volume of low-cost competitors drives prices down; positioning as premium is difficult.

resistance_patterns.name: Payment Rail Friction
resistance_patterns.description: International payment collection via PayPal, Wise, Payoneer adds friction and fees.

opportunity_patterns.name: Income Arbitrage Opportunity
opportunity_patterns.description: Skilled workers in emerging markets can earn 5-10x local rates by serving global clients.

opportunity_patterns.name: AI Tool Leverage
opportunity_patterns.description: AI coding, design, and writing tools dramatically increase output per freelancer.

opportunity_patterns.name: Freelancer Community and Education Market
opportunity_patterns.description: 50M+ freelancers need courses, tools, and community support.

trust_mechanisms.name: Review History is Everything
trust_mechanisms.description: Star ratings, client testimonials, and portfolio work are the primary trust signal.

trust_mechanisms.name: Niche Expertise Signaling
trust_mechanisms.description: Deep specialization in a specific technology or domain signals expertise faster.

payment_patterns.name: Escrow-Based Project Payments
payment_patterns.description: Platform escrow (Upwork) or milestone-based payment is standard.

payment_patterns.name: Payoneer, Wise, PayPal Withdrawal
payment_patterns.description: Multiple payout options but all carry fees; bank transfer is cheapest at scale.

institutional_patterns.name: Platform as Labor Market Regulator
institutional_patterns.description: Upwork, Fiverr, Toptal set rules, enforce quality, and manage payment disputes.

institutional_patterns.name: Tax Compliance Complexity
institutional_patterns.description: International income creates tax complexity in both client and freelancer jurisdictions.

narrative_patterns.name: Portfolio and Case Study Power
narrative_patterns.description: Work samples and case studies are primary sales collateral.

narrative_patterns.name: Thought Leadership as Lead Generation
narrative_patterns.description: Sharing expertise publicly generates inbound leads.

platform_patterns.name: Upwork and Fiverr as Primary Marketplaces
platform_patterns.description: These platforms control the primary discovery layer for freelance work.

platform_patterns.name: LinkedIn for Direct Client Acquisition
platform_patterns.description: LinkedIn increasingly used to bypass platform fees through direct outreach.

regulatory_patterns.name: Foreign Income Tax Obligations
regulatory_patterns.description: Income from foreign clients often taxable in both countries.

regulatory_patterns.name: Platform Terms of Service
regulatory_patterns.description: Platform TOS can ban entire categories of work or penalize off-platform billing.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Portfolio and Sample-Driven Hiring
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Clients hire based on portfolio, not interviews or credentials.

customer_behavior_patterns.name: Fixed-Price Project Preference
customer_behavior_patterns.description: Most clients prefer fixed-price projects over hourly to control budget.

business_model_fit.notes: Best for freelancer platforms, tools, and education businesses.

common_failure_modes.name: Generalist Positioning
common_failure_modes.description: Positioning as 'web developer' rather than 'Shopify conversion optimization specialist'.

common_failure_modes.name: Platform Fee Avoidance
common_failure_modes.description: Taking clients off-platform to avoid fees violates TOS and loses protection.

common_success_patterns.name: Hyper-Specific Niche Claim
common_success_patterns.description: Owning one very specific keyword and problem set before expanding.

common_success_patterns.name: Retainer Conversion from Project
common_success_patterns.description: Converting one-time projects into monthly retainer relationships.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: Upwork Profile Optimization First
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Build Upwork profile with portfolio, specialized service offering, and competitive initial pricing.

recommended_entry_strategies.name: First Clients at Loss-Leader Price
recommended_entry_strategies.description: Accept first 3-5 projects at very low rates to build review history.

source_notes: Based on global freelance digital economy characteristics.

name: SaaS Startup
short_description: Subscription software ecosystems with product-market fit obsession, churn risk, and VC-fueled growth dynamics.
long_description: The SaaS startup economy is a global phenomenon concentrated in certain hubs (SF Bay Area, NYC, London, Tel Aviv, Bangalore, Tallinn) but operating globally. Subscription software businesses compete on product-market fit, net revenue retention, and growth metrics. VC funding cycles heavily influence market dynamics. Customer success is the primary retention mechanism. Competition is intense; commoditization is constant.
core_characteristic: Subscription software, product-market fit, churn risk

resistance_patterns.name: Feature Parity Commoditization
resistance_patterns.description: Core SaaS features are rapidly commoditized; differentiation requires constant innovation.

resistance_patterns.name: Customer Acquisition Cost Inflation
resistance_patterns.description: Cost to acquire B2B customers is rising across all channels.

resistance_patterns.name: Churn Rate Pressure
resistance_patterns.description: Monthly or annual churn must stay below threshold or growth is impossible.

opportunity_patterns.name: AI-Native Product Disruption
opportunity_patterns.description: AI-native alternatives to existing SaaS categories creating new market entries.

opportunity_patterns.name: Vertical SaaS Opportunity
opportunity_patterns.description: Industry-specific SaaS with deep vertical integration commands premium pricing.

opportunity_patterns.name: International Market Expansion
opportunity_patterns.description: Many SaaS categories remain under-served in non-US markets.

trust_mechanisms.name: G2 and Capterra Reviews
trust_mechanisms.description: Software review platforms are critical discovery and trust mechanism.

trust_mechanisms.name: SOC2 and Compliance Certifications
trust_mechanisms.description: Enterprise buyers require security certifications before evaluating products.

payment_patterns.name: Stripe Subscription Infrastructure
payment_patterns.description: Stripe dominates SaaS billing infrastructure globally.

payment_patterns.name: Annual vs Monthly Billing Trade-off
payment_patterns.description: Annual billing improves cash flow; monthly billing reduces adoption friction.

institutional_patterns.name: VC Funding Cycle Dependency
institutional_patterns.description: SaaS ecosystem is heavily influenced by VC availability and interest rate cycles.

institutional_patterns.name: Cloud Provider Ecosystem
institutional_patterns.description: AWS, GCP, Azure marketplace presence influences enterprise sales.

narrative_patterns.name: 10x ROI Narrative
narrative_patterns.description: B2B SaaS must clearly articulate quantifiable ROI for buyer justification.

narrative_patterns.name: Category Creation vs Category Entry
narrative_patterns.description: Category-creating companies command premium valuations and attention.

name: Cybercrime / Dark Web
short_description: Hostile digital actor networks operating outside all legal frameworks with fraud, hacking, and underground commerce.
long_description: The cybercrime dark web economy is a global network of hostile digital actors engaged in fraud, ransomware, data theft, scam operations, and underground commerce. It operates through anonymizing networks (Tor), cryptocurrency payments, and dark web marketplaces. This is not a target market — it is a hostile operating environment that any legitimate business faces. Understanding it is about defense, not offense. Products sold to consumers in regions with high cybercrime pressure must account for fraud, account takeover, and identity theft as design constraints.
